The account received large credits of Rs.110,000 on August 13, 2026, and Rs.140,000 on August 14, 2026, via UPI from unknown counterparties A and B, respectively. On August 15, 2026, a debit of Rs.246,500 was made to UPI handle C, which is flagged in the I4C Suspect Registry. Another debit of Rs.94,200 was made to the same flagged counterparty on August 17, 2026. The pattern is inconsistent with the customer's declared monthly income of Rs.28,000 and low-risk profile.

The transactions trigger POE-003 (Transaction History) due to multiple large credits and debits within a short period, with a total credit of Rs.3.45L. POE-004 (Customer Risk Profile) is triggered as the customer's low-risk profile does not align with the high-risk transactions. POE-005 (Income Level) is also triggered, as the total credits are 12 times the customer's declared monthly income. The transactions show a pass-through pattern, with 98.8% of the credits immediately passed to a flagged counterparty, triggering POE-007 (Beneficiary). POE-008 (Transaction Frequency) and POE-009 (Transaction Size) are triggered due to multiple large transactions within a short period, which are not consistent with the customer's income or profile. POE-010 (Transaction Complexity) is triggered due to the complex pattern of credits and debits involving unknown and flagged counterparties.

The record does not rule out the possibility that the customer may have a legitimate business or income source not declared. However, it contradicts the explanation that the customer's transactions are consistent with their declared income and low-risk profile, given the large credits and debits to/from unknown and flagged counterparties. The transactions are reportable under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, Section 12(1)(b), as they may indicate a transaction involving proceeds of crime.

The account received three cash deposits on 2026-08-19, totaling Rs.420000, with two deposits of Rs.142500 each from ACCT-02-A and ACCT-02-B, and one deposit of Rs.135000 from ACCT-02-C. The next day, Rs.420000 was debited via NEFT to a single current account at another bank. This pattern is inconsistent with the customer's declared income of Rs.10K/month and their profile as a daily labourer. 

The transactions trigger multiple red-flag indicators, including the pass-through pattern and the I4C flag, as evidenced by the large cash deposits below the CTR threshold, followed by a large NEFT transaction. The POE factors triggered include POE-003, as multiple cash deposits were made on the same day, POE-004, due to the customer having three linked savings accounts at the same branch, POE-005, as the customer's declared income does not align with the large cash deposits, POE-007, due to the beneficiary being a single current account at a different bank, POE-008, as multiple cash deposits were made on the same day and a subsequent NEFT transaction occurred the next day, POE-009, due to the large cash deposits and NEFT transaction, and POE-010, as the use of multiple accounts and cash deposits below the CTR threshold, followed by a large NEFT transaction, suggests complexity.

The record does not rule out innocent explanations, such as the customer receiving legitimate payments, but it contradicts explanations that the customer's income and transactions are consistent with their declared profile, given the large cash deposits and subsequent NEFT transaction. The statutory basis for this report is Section 12(1)(b) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.

The account received six large cash deposits at the branch counter between 2026-08-10 and 2026-08-21, totaling Rs.85L, after being dormant for three years. The deposits were Rs.14.5L on 2026-08-10, Rs.12L on 2026-08-11, Rs.15L on 2026-08-13, Rs.13.5L on 2026-08-17, Rs.16L on 2026-08-19, and Rs.14L on 2026-08-21. This pattern is inconsistent with the customer's declared profile as a 71-year-old retired government employee with a monthly pension of Rs.35K. The total amount deposited exceeds the customer's annual pension by a significant margin, triggering POE-005 (Income Level). The frequency and size of the transactions also trigger POE-008 (Transaction Frequency) and POE-009 (Transaction Size), respectively. The sudden activity in a previously dormant account raises concerns, as indicated by POE-003 (Transaction History) and POE-004 (Customer Risk Profile). The record does not rule out the possibility that the customer received these funds as a one-time inheritance or gift, but it contradicts the explanation that the deposits are related to the customer's regular pension income, given the large amounts and short timeframe. The RFI-003 alert signal further highlights the unusual nature of these transactions. Pursuant to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, section 12(1)(b), these transactions warrant reporting due to the suspicious pattern and inconsistency with the customer's known profile.

The account received multiple large credits via NEFT from various construction companies, including Rs. 850,000 on 2026-06-15 from ABC Infrastructure Ltd, Rs. 620,000 on 2026-06-20 from DEF Engineering Pvt Ltd, and Rs. 1,100,000 on 2026-07-15 from ABC Infrastructure Ltd. This pattern is inconsistent with the customer's declared profile as a state PWD engineer with a monthly income of Rs. 95,000. The credits from construction companies, such as DEF Engineering Pvt Ltd and GHI Constructions, may indicate undisclosed income sources, triggering POE-006 (Source of Income). The frequent large credits, including Rs. 930,000 on 2026-08-15 from DEF Engineering Pvt Ltd and Rs. 820,000 on 2026-08-20 from JKL Roadways Pvt Ltd, exceed the customer's declared income, triggering POE-005 (Income Level) and POE-009 (Transaction Size).

The record does not rule out the possibility that the customer has a legitimate business relationship with these companies, but it contradicts the customer's declared income and occupation, as evidenced by the large credits from multiple construction companies. The pattern of transactions, including the credits from ABC Infrastructure Ltd, DEF Engineering Pvt Ltd, and GHI Constructions, triggers POE-003 (Transaction History) and POE-008 (Transaction Frequency). The customer's PEP status and medium-high risk profile, as well as the potential KYC deficiencies, trigger POE-004 (Customer Risk Profile) and POE-012 (KYC Availability).

The red-flag indicators RFI-009 and RFI-006 are triggered due to the large and frequent credits from construction companies. The statutory basis for this report is Section 12(1)(b) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), which requires reporting of transactions that may indicate money laundering. The transactions in question, including the large credits from construction companies, may be related to money laundering activities.

The account of an IT services exporter with a declared annual turnover of Rs.4.2Cr and a Medium risk profile has been involved in two large outward payments. On 2026-08-06, a debit transaction of Rs.37.5L was made to Regal Trading FZCO, Sharjah, UAE, via a DPRK-linked correspondent using the SWIFT channel. Another debit transaction of Rs.26.7L was made to the same counterparty on 2026-08-27, also via SWIFT. 

The pattern of these transactions is inconsistent with the customer's declared profile as an IT services exporter, given the large amounts and the involvement of a DPRK-linked correspondent. The transactions trigger several red-flag indicators, including POE-002 (Business Profile), as the customer's business does not typically involve large outward payments to a UAE-based company via a DPRK-linked correspondent. POE-003 (Transaction History) is also triggered due to the two large outward SWIFT payments within a short period. Additionally, POE-007 (Beneficiary) and POE-010 (Transaction Complexity) are triggered due to the payments made to Regal Trading FZCO and the routing via a DPRK-linked correspondent.

The record does not rule out innocent explanations such as legitimate business transactions, but it contradicts the expectation that an IT services exporter with a Medium risk profile would typically engage in such large and complex transactions. The transactions also trigger POE-004 (Customer Risk Profile), POE-008 (Transaction Frequency), and POE-009 (Transaction Size) due to the customer's risk classification and the size and frequency of the transactions. 

The statutory basis for this report is Section 12(1)(b) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), which mandates the reporting of transactions that may involve proceeds of crime. The transactions in question, involving large outward payments to a company linked to a DPRK-linked correspondent, warrant further examination.
